title: Keep private details out of a chatbot

cards.text: CISA says not to share sensitive information with AI tools. Keep personal details, like your bank number, out of a chatbot.
cards.line: Some details belong only with people you trust.

cards.text: CISA says AI systems learn from what users enter. If you would not post a detail for everyone to see, do not put it into a chatbot.
CISA says not to rely only on AI answers. Check important answers another way, such as with an official site or a trusted person.
cards.line: A second check can catch a wrong answer.

checks.prompt: Which detail should stay out of a chatbot?
checks.why: CISA says not to share private details with AI tools.

checks.prompt: You want to share a detail with an AI tool. What question can help?
options: Would I post this for everyone to see?
Is this detail short enough to type?
Will the tool answer in one sentence?
checks.answer: Would I post this for everyone to see?
checks.why: CISA says that if you would not post it on social media, you should not share it with an AI tool.

checks.prompt: An AI answer affects an important choice. What should you do?
options: Send it to a friend without checking
checks.why: CISA says AI is a tool, not a replacement for your own skills. Checking another way is a safe habit.

takeaway: Keep private details out of chatbots and check important answers a second way.

sources.name: CISA Secure Our World, Stay safe online when using AI (tip sheet)
CISA, Secure Our World and Cybersecurity Awareness Month resources (archive)

situations.text: You would not post your home address for everyone to see. Should you type it into an AI tool?
situations.why: CISA says if you would not post it, do not share it with an AI tool.

situations.text: You ask an AI tool for a simple soup recipe.
situations.why: A recipe has no private details in it.

situations.text: An answer from an AI tool never needs a second check.
situations.why: CISA says not to rely only on AI answers. Check important ones another way.
